suggestions.title: Log Saturday. Rough numbers are fine — it is the one day that decides this week's question.

rationale.science: When a rate stalls, logging drift and portion creep explain it far more often than metabolism — and metabolic adaptation is real but modest, roughly 50-100 calories a day for moderate loss (Alhassan 2008; Nunes 2021). Adherence is checked before the metabolism is blamed, not after.
rationale.data: dailyLogs runs 8/10, 8/11, 8/12, 8/13, 8/14 and stops — 8/15 has no entry at all, and no sleep night either. Your own lab read on this file: Saturday owns 8 of your 17 logging misses, and weekend protein hits run 50% against 81% on weekdays.
rationale.relationship: Friday finally landed at 2,800 against a Monday-to-Thursday mean of 2,242 — 558 high, and the first day in the file that behaves the way the under-logging case says it should. One such day is not a pattern. Two would be. Saturday is the day that tells us which, and it is also the day your record is historically least likely to hold.

suggestions.predict: If 8/15 comes in within about 150 calories of your Monday-to-Thursday mean, the log is holding and I move my suspicion onto my own maintenance fit, which has already slid 2,886 to 2,646 in five days. If it comes in near Friday's number, then two of your last seven days ran well above the rest and the week's real average was never what the four clean days said. A blank Saturday is the only outcome that tells us nothing.

suggestions.title: Pick the hip-thrust starting load before Monday — it has no weight on file and you skipped it Thursday.

rationale.science: On a cut you defend load rather than chase volume, and working sets want to land around 1-3 reps in reserve (Schoenfeld 2017; Robinson 2024). A debut set at a load nobody chose is a hard set spent on nothing, and it sets the baseline every future session gets graded against.
rationale.data: exercises.hipthrust is on file with w: null, created 8/12, inserted 8/17 — which is Monday, a lower day. It was already on Thursday's lower day and appears in that session's skipped list. The machine fly has the same blank, but it does not come up until Thursday's upper day.
rationale.relationship: You have run this exact play twice and it went both ways. The hack debut was picked on the floor, came back wrong, and the 170 rung is on the record as RETRACTED. The ham 125 got checked in SETUP first and debuted clean at 11,9,9. Monday is a bad day to guess: it is the same session that re-baselines eleven other lifts, so a mis-loaded debut is the one number nobody will be able to untangle later.

suggestions.predict: Set the load beforehand and the hip thrust draws an honest first entry Monday with a baseline that is usable from session one. Leave it blank and I expect it to come in obviously mis-loaded and need a weight correction on the day, the way hack did on 8/14 — or to get skipped a second time, which is the same outcome with fewer steps. Grade it on whether hipthrust has a w value and an entry in Monday's sessionLog.
